model.name: Dependency / Impact
model.purpose: Provide format-neutral graph-analysis semantics for typed dependency and downstream impact: preserve asserted edges as primary facts, express every derived graph result as a declared projection over a named snapshot, state when an edge licenses impact propagation and when it must be excluded, and forbid absence or non-reachability conclusions that are not backed by an explicit completeness declaration.
model.scope_statement: This bounded pass covers only the graph-analysis surface of WM-XCT-037. In scope: the asserted dependency edge as an addressable primary fact (typed, directed, scoped, time-bounded, provenance- and confidence-bearing); the modality distinction between direct, transitive, inferred and hypothetical relations; propagation licensing and exclusion rules keyed on edge type, condition, lifecycle scope, time and confidence; completeness and closed-world declarations that must precede any absence or reachability conclusion; and derived results (paths, cycles, strongly connected groups, fan-in, fan-out, cut sets, reachability sets, alternative paths) recorded as projections carrying algorithm identity, parameters, edge filter and input snapshot digest. The model is a mixin applied to a host subject: it never owns the identity or inventory of the entities it connects, never executes graph algorithms, and never schedules or performs change.
in_scope: Asserted dependency edge as an immutable primary fact with typed direction, lifecycle scope, validity window, assertion provenance and confidence
Modality discrimination so that direct, transitive, inferred and hypothetical relations are never conflated in a stored statement or an answer
Propagation licensing: the explicit conditions under which impact may traverse an edge, and typed exclusions when it must not (type, condition, scope, time, confidence)
Completeness and closed-world declarations, enumeration frontier and declared known unknowns as preconditions for any absence, non-reachability or 'no impact' claim

Derived graph results as declared projections: path semantics and path modes, cycle and strongly-connected-group detection, fan-in and fan-out degree, cut sets, reachability sets and alternative or disjoint paths
Projection provenance: algorithm identifier and version, parameters, edge-selection filter, input snapshot digest, run time, determinism class and supersession
out_of_scope: Graph storage, indexing and query execution: a graph database, triple store, GQL engine or in-memory projection library is an interface and storage projection, not part of these semantics

Identity, versioning, classification and inventory completeness of the entities at the edge endpoints; those belong to the owning component or asset inventory model and are carried here only by reference
Execution of graph algorithms, entailment computation and reasoner materialisation; this model records what a run declared, never performs it
Change scheduling, release orchestration, remediation planning and any change execution triggered by an impact result
Vulnerability adjudication, exploitability decisions, risk scoring and probability quantification; cut sets and path sets are recorded as method-declared results, not as risk verdicts
Access enforcement and audit-trail generation; this model declares only the metadata a released projection must carry so an external audit record can be correlated
Physical erasure, legal hold and retention execution over stored records
Domain-specific dependency vocabularies (build systems, supply chain, network topology, organisational dependency) beyond binding them by reference as governed edge-type codes

boundary_notes.neighbor: Graph query engine and graph database (ISO/IEC 39075 GQL)
boundary_notes.distinction: GQL normatively defines graph pattern matching, path patterns and path restrictors as a query language executed by an engine. This model consumes those distinctions as declarative labels on a recorded result (which path mode, which bound, which selection), so that a stored projection is interpretable without the engine. It does not define query syntax, evaluation order, indexing or execution plans.

PROV owns how an entity came to be, through activities, agents, generation and usage. This model owns the dependency edge and its analysis semantics. Critically, PROV-CONSTRAINTS states there is no inference making derivation transitive and shows wasInformedBy is non-transitive; this model therefore refuses to inherit transitivity by default and requires an explicit declared basis for every transitive or inferred relation.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Component inventory and SBOM models (SPDX 3.0.1, CycloneDX 1.6)
boundary_notes.distinction: Those specifications own element identity, component metadata and document-level inventory. This mixin reuses their relationship semantics (typed from/to relationship, completeness, lifecycle scope, dependsOn/provides) as alignment targets for the edge, and holds endpoints only as resolvable references into the owning inventory.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Reliability and risk analysis models (IEC 61025 fault tree analysis, IEC 61078 reliability block diagrams)
boundary_notes.distinction: Those standards own deductive failure modelling, cut-set derivation procedures, redundancy structures and quantitative dependability computation. This model records a cut set, path set or criticality measure as a projection that names the method and its inputs; it never computes or interprets failure probability, importance factors or risk acceptance.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Ontology reasoner and entailment regime (OWL 2, RDF 1.1 Semantics)
boundary_notes.distinction: OWL 2 owns property characteristics such as TransitiveObjectProperty and property chains together with the global restrictions that keep reasoning decidable; RDF 1.1 Semantics establishes that a valid inference does not oblige any application to materialise it. This model records which characteristic or chain licensed an inferred edge and whether it was materialised; it does not perform entailment or claim conformance to any entailment regime.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Exploitability and exception statement models (VEX / OpenVEX)
boundary_notes.distinction: OpenVEX owns vulnerability status and its justifications for a product-vulnerability pair. This model borrows only the shape of a machine-readable justification to express edge-level propagation exclusion (for example, present but not on the execute path), and cites the external statement by reference. Vulnerability status, remediation and disclosure remain outside.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Change, release and remediation execution model
boundary_notes.distinction: An impact projection is an input to change planning. Deciding, scheduling, approving or executing a change, and recording that execution, belongs to the change model. Lifecycle scope on an edge (design, build, test, runtime) qualifies the dependency assertion; it does not grant this model any workflow or executor role.

sources.title: Relationship - SPDX Specification 3.0.1 (Core model, Relationship class)
sources.relevance: Normative shape of an asserted, addressable relationship: exactly one from Element, one or more to Elements, one relationshipType, optional completeness, optional startTime and endTime marking when the relationship became and ceased to be valid; NoneElement asserts no relationships exist while NoAssertionElement covers undeterminable existence.

sources.title: RelationshipCompleteness - SPDX Specification 3.0.1
sources.relevance: Three-valued completeness vocabulary: complete ('known to be exhaustive'), incomplete ('known not to be exhaustive') and noAssertion. Direct normative basis for requiring an explicit completeness declaration before any closed-world or absence conclusion.

sources.title: LifecycleScopeType - SPDX Specification 3.0.1
sources.relevance: Enumerates design, development, build, test, runtime and other as contexts for dependency relationships, with the explicit rationale that 'a build dependency may have different implications than an operational dependency'. Grounds scope-conditioned propagation licensing.

sources.title: Constraints of the PROV Data Model (PROV-CONSTRAINTS)
sources.relevance: States that there is no inference making wasDerivedFrom transitive and gives a timing counterexample showing wasInformedBy is not transitive; defines ordering constraints (generation before usage, start before end) and impossibility constraints. Authority for treating transitivity as a declared, not assumed, property.

sources.title: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Structural Specification and Functional-Style Syntax (Second Edition)
sources.relevance: Defines TransitiveObjectProperty and SubObjectPropertyOf with object property chains, plus the Section 11 global restrictions limiting where composite and transitive properties may be used in OWL 2 DL. Grounds the declared derivation basis for inferred and transitive edges and the need to bound closure.

sources.title: RDF 1.1 Semantics
sources.relevance: Defines entailment ('a graph G simply entails a graph E when every interpretation which satisfies G also satisfies E') and states that a valid inference does not oblige any application to make it, and that RDF is a purely assertional language. Basis for separating asserted facts from optionally materialised derived statements and for refusing absence semantics.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 39075:2024 Information technology - Database languages - GQL
sources.relevance: International standard for property-graph querying that normatively defines graph pattern matching, path patterns, match modes and path restrictors (walk, trail, acyclic, simple). Used here only as the alignment vocabulary for declaring which path semantics a recorded result assumed. Full normative text is paywalled; catalogue entry verified.

sources.title: CycloneDX Bill of Materials Specification, Protocol Buffers schema bom-1.6.proto (Dependency message)
sources.relevance: Defines ref, dependsOn and provides, and states that 'Components or services that are not represented in the dependency graph may have unknown dependencies. It is recommended that implementations assume this to be opaque and not an indicator of an object being dependency-free.' Direct authority for the opaque-absence rule.

sources.title: OpenVEX Specification
sources.relevance: Machine-readable justification labels (component_not_present, vulnerable_code_not_present, vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path, vulnerable_code_cannot_be_controlled_by_adversary, inline_mitigations_already_exist) and the product/subcomponent structure. Model for typed edge-level propagation exclusion distinct from edge absence.

sources.title: IEC 61025:2006 Fault tree analysis (FTA)
sources.relevance: International standard for deductive top-down impact analysis; defines top event, intermediate and basic events, cut sets and minimal cut sets, and identification rules and symbols. Authority for cut-set results and for the requirement that assumptions and event boundaries be identified explicitly.

sources.title: IEC 61078:2016 Reliability block diagrams
sources.relevance: Standard for modelling dependability with success-path structures, covering qualitative and quantitative analysis, non-coherent and dynamic diagrams, Boolean algebra methods, and the stated relationship with fault tree analysis (IEC 61025) and Markov techniques. Authority for alternative-path and redundancy semantics as the dual of cut sets.

sources.title: Strongly Connected Components - Neo4j Graph Data Science documentation
sources.version_or_date: Graph Data Science, current documentation (versions 2.5 through 2026.07)
sources.relevance: Working definition of strongly connected components ('a set is considered a strongly connected component if there is a directed path between each pair of nodes within the set') and the operational pattern of computing over a named in-memory graph projection with stream, stats, mutate and write modes, where results reflect the projected graph at execution time. Used as implementation evidence for snapshot-bound projections, not as normative authority.

sources.title: Framing Software Component Transparency: Establishing a Common Software Bill of Materials (SBOM), Third Edition
sources.relevance: Public-authority framing that further defines and clarifies SBOM attributes, establishing that component and dependency relationship transparency is an expected attribute set rather than an optional analytic convenience. Cited only for that framing; the PDF body could not be machine-parsed in this pass.

bundles.name: Asserted edge base and propagation gating
bundles.description: The primary-fact layer of the dependency graph: what an asserted edge is, how it stays addressable and immutable, how derived or postulated relations are kept distinguishable from it, and the explicit gate that decides whether impact may travel along an edge at all.
bundles.rationale: Every defensible impact answer resolves to a set of asserted edges plus a rule that permitted traversal. SPDX 3.0.1 models a relationship as an addressable assertion with from, to, type, completeness and a validity interval; SPDX lifecycle scope records that a build dependency and an operational dependency have different implications; OpenVEX shows that a present component can still be non-impacting for a stated reason. PROV-CONSTRAINTS and RDF 1.1 Semantics jointly forbid assuming transitivity or materialisation. Grouping these into one bundle keeps the fact base auditable and prevents propagation policy from leaking into stored facts.

layers.name: Edge assertion and relation modality
layers.description: How a single dependency edge is asserted, addressed, typed, scoped and time-bounded, and how direct, transitive, inferred and hypothetical relations remain separable in storage and in answers.

findings.name: Asserted dependency edge as a primary fact
findings.description: An asserted edge is a first-class, addressable statement that a source subject depends on one or more target subjects under a named relation type, a lifecycle scope, a validity interval, an asserting agent and a confidence value. It is treated as immutable: corrections are made by superseding assertions, never by silent edit, so that any projection computed over an earlier edge set remains explainable. Endpoints are references into an owning inventory model, never copies of the entities.

questions.text: What identifier makes this asserted dependency edge addressable independently of its endpoints?
answer_data: Composite edge key over source reference, relation type, target reference, lifecycle scope and validity start
Master-system assertion identifier or governed IRI where the asserting system issues one
Minting authority and scheme for locally assigned surrogate identifiers

questions.text: Which typed relation does the edge assert, in which direction, and under which lifecycle scope?
answer_data: Relation type code drawn from a governed vocabulary such as SPDX RelationshipType or CycloneDX dependsOn/provides
Direction convention fixing which endpoint is the dependant and which is the dependency
Zero or more lifecycle scope codes (design, development, build, test, runtime, other)

questions.text: Over which validity interval is the asserted edge held to be true, and when was that observed?
answer_data: Edge start time and end time as RFC 3339 values with explicit offset or Z
Separate assertion or observation timestamp for when the claim was recorded
Marker for an open-ended or unknown interval end

questions.text: Who or what asserted the edge, from which evidence, and with what confidence?
answer_data: Asserting agent, tool or document reference
Evidence reference such as a build manifest, scan result, declared dependency file or human declaration
Confidence value together with the identifier of the scale that defines it

questions.text: How do the edge endpoints resolve to entities owned by an external inventory model?
answer_data: Endpoint reference scheme (SPDX Element identifier, CycloneDX bom-ref, purl, CPE, master-data key)
Identifier of the inventory or asset model that owns each endpoint
Behaviour when an endpoint reference fails to resolve, including quarantine rather than silent drop

data_elements.name: Edge key
data_elements.description: Stable, date-free identifier for the asserted edge, resolved by the identity priority rule.

data_elements.name: Source endpoint reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the dependant subject, owned by an external inventory model.

data_elements.name: Target endpoint reference
data_elements.description: One or more references to depended-on subjects; a distinguished none-marker asserts that no such dependency exists, and is not the same as omission.

data_elements.name: Relation type code
data_elements.description: Governed code for the asserted relation, bound to an external vocabulary by namespace.

data_elements.name: Lifecycle scope
data_elements.description: Zero or more lifecycle contexts in which the dependency holds, following the SPDX lifecycle scope vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Edge validity window
data_elements.description: Start and end of the interval over which the asserted edge is claimed valid, recorded separately from assertion time.

data_elements.name: Assertion provenance
data_elements.description: Asserting agent or tool, evidence references and assertion timestamp for the edge.

data_elements.name: Assertion confidence
data_elements.description: Confidence attached to the edge assertion, with an explicit scale reference; consumed by propagation licensing thresholds.

artifacts.name: Edge assertion record
artifacts.description: The format-neutral record of one asserted dependency edge, carrying key, endpoints, type, scope, validity window, provenance and confidence, plus any supersession pointer. Projectable to an SPDX Relationship, a CycloneDX dependency entry, a reified RDF statement or a property-graph edge without loss of the declared semantics.
media_or_form: structured record, format-neutral
projection to SPDX 3.0.1 Relationship
projection to CycloneDX 1.6 dependency entry
projection to a qualified RDF statement or property-graph edge
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative master-system assertion identifier where the asserting system of record issues one; otherwise a governed IRI from a published namespace; otherwise a Dimension-minted UUID or ULID recorded with its minting authority. The composite edge key is retained as a natural key for deduplication but never replaces the assigned identifier.

findings.name: Direct, transitive, inferred and hypothetical modality
findings.description: Every dependency statement carries a modality discriminator plus, for non-direct modalities, the basis that licensed it. Direct means asserted by an agent about an immediate relation. Transitive means produced by composing asserted edges under a declared closure with a stated depth bound. Inferred means entailed by a declared property characteristic, property chain or rule. Hypothetical means postulated for what-if analysis and not claimed to hold. PROV-CONSTRAINTS establishes that derivation is not transitive by default, and RDF 1.1 Semantics establishes that a valid inference need not be materialised, so both transitivity and materialisation must be declared rather than assumed.

questions.text: How are direct, transitive, inferred and hypothetical relations defined so that they never collapse into one another?
answer_data: Closed modality vocabulary with one definition per term and mutually exclusive assignment
Rule that a statement carries exactly one modality and that modality survives export to any storage projection
Prohibition on promoting a derived statement to direct without a new agent assertion

questions.text: For an inferred or transitive relation, which rule, property characteristic or closure method licensed it?
answer_data: Reference to a declared transitive property or object property chain, with the OWL 2 global-restriction check recorded
Closure method identifier and the traversal depth actually applied
Ordered list of asserted edge keys consumed as premises

questions.text: Is a derived relation materialised as a stored statement, and how is it kept distinguishable from asserted facts?
answer_data: Materialisation flag with the projection or run that produced the statement
Storage rule keeping derived statements outside the asserted edge set
Invalidation trigger when a premise edge is superseded or its validity window closes

questions.text: Under what conditions may a hypothetical relation enter an impact answer, and how is that answer labelled?
answer_data: Scenario identifier that scopes the hypothetical edge set
Mandatory labelling of any answer that consumed hypothetical edges
Default exclusion of hypothetical edges from actual-state answers

data_elements.name: Relation modality
data_elements.description: Discriminator with values direct, transitive, inferred or hypothetical, carried on every dependency statement.

data_elements.name: Derivation basis
data_elements.description: For transitive or inferred statements: the property characteristic, property chain, rule or closure method reference plus the depth applied and the premise edge keys.

data_elements.name: Materialisation flag
data_elements.description: Whether the derived statement is stored or is recomputed on demand; a valid inference does not oblige materialisation.

data_elements.name: Hypothesis scenario reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of the what-if scenario that scopes a hypothetical edge, including which edges it adds or removes.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Modality is a discriminator and a small justification structure carried on records that already exist elsewhere in the model: the edge assertion record for asserted facts and the analysis run descriptor and result sets for derived statements. Materialising it as its own artifact would create a second addressable object for the same statement and would immediately raise a synchronisation problem between the artifact and the statement it qualifies. The controlled modality vocabulary and the property-characteristic definitions it points to are governed outside this model, in OWL 2 and in the adopting Dimension's namespace registry, so this finding contributes constraints and reference bindings rather than a stored artifact of its own.

layers.name: Propagation licensing and exclusion
layers.description: The explicit gate that decides whether impact may traverse an asserted edge: positive licence profiles keyed on type, scope, direction, condition and confidence, and negative typed exclusions that suppress a present edge for a stated and evidenced reason.

findings.name: Conditions under which an edge licenses propagation
findings.description: An edge is a fact; it is not automatically a channel for impact. A propagation licence profile states which combinations of relation type, lifecycle scope, direction, validity overlap and minimum confidence permit traversal for a given impact question. Because SPDX records that a build dependency carries different implications from an operational dependency, the same asserted edge can license propagation in one scope and not in another. The default is deny: an edge that matches no profile is not traversed, and the resulting answer says so rather than silently omitting a branch.

questions.text: Which combination of relation type, lifecycle scope and direction licenses impact to propagate along an edge?
answer_data: Licence profile matching relation type codes to permitted propagation directions
Lifecycle scopes in which the licence applies and those in which it is withheld
Impact question class the profile is written for, since one profile does not serve every question

questions.text: What is the default when no propagation licence profile matches an edge?
answer_data: Explicit deny-by-default rule with no implicit fallback
Required reporting of unmatched edges as a distinct category in the result
Escalation path for requesting a new profile

questions.text: What minimum assertion confidence must an edge carry before it may be traversed for a published impact answer?
answer_data: Confidence threshold per profile and the scale it is expressed on
Treatment of edges with absent confidence values
Whether below-threshold edges are dropped or reported as a separate low-confidence frontier

questions.text: How must an edge validity window overlap the analysis reference time for traversal to be permitted?
answer_data: Reference instant or interval the analysis is asked about
Overlap predicate (contains, intersects, starts-before) applied to edge validity windows
Handling of edges with open or unknown interval ends

questions.text: Who owns and versions a propagation licence profile, and how are competing profiles resolved?
answer_data: Owning role and approval record for each profile version
Deterministic precedence rule when several profiles match the same edge
Change class that makes a profile revision breaking for existing projections

data_elements.name: Propagation licence profile identifier
data_elements.description: Versioned identifier of the profile that governs traversal for a class of impact questions.

data_elements.name: Licensed relation types
data_elements.description: Relation type codes the profile permits to be traversed.

data_elements.name: Permitted propagation direction
data_elements.description: Whether impact may travel along the edge downstream, upstream or in both directions for this profile.

data_elements.name: Licence condition
data_elements.description: Additional predicate that must hold for traversal, such as a configuration flag, deployment condition or lifecycle scope match.

data_elements.name: Confidence threshold
data_elements.description: Minimum edge assertion confidence required by the profile, with its scale reference.

artifacts.name: Propagation licence profile
artifacts.description: A versioned, format-neutral rule set binding relation types, lifecycle scopes, directions, temporal overlap predicates and confidence thresholds to a permission to traverse for a named class of impact question, together with its deny-by-default statement and precedence rank.
media_or_form: versioned rule set, format-neutral
tabular decision matrix over relation type and lifecycle scope
declarative predicate document referenced by an analysis run
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed profile identifier issued by the owning package in the adopting Dimension's namespace, with an explicit semantic version; date-free. Superseded versions remain resolvable so historical projections stay interpretable.

findings.name: Typed exclusion of a present edge
findings.description: An edge that exists and matches a licence profile may still be excluded from a specific impact answer for a stated, evidenced reason. OpenVEX demonstrates the pattern with machine-readable justifications such as the vulnerable code not being present, not being on the execute path, not being controllable by an adversary, or being covered by inline mitigations. Generalised here, an exclusion is a typed, scoped, expiring statement over an edge, an edge class or a subgraph. The critical rule is reporting: an excluded edge must be visible in the result as suppressed, never rendered as absent, because absence carries a completeness claim that an exclusion does not.

questions.text: Which machine-readable justification explains why a present edge does not propagate impact in this case?
answer_data: Justification code from a governed vocabulary aligned to OpenVEX status justifications
Free-text elaboration bound to the code, never replacing it
Rule that an exclusion without a justification code is invalid

questions.text: What is the applicability scope of an exclusion and when does it lapse?
answer_data: Scope as a single edge, a relation-type class, a subgraph or an endpoint neighbourhood
Effective-from and expiry timestamps in RFC 3339 with offset
Re-review trigger when a premise edge or configuration changes

questions.text: What evidence supports the exclusion and who reviewed it?
answer_data: Evidence references such as configuration proof, call-graph analysis or build settings
Reviewing role and approval record
Evidence strength or confidence recorded on the same scale as edge confidence

questions.text: How is an excluded edge reported so that a consumer can tell suppression from absence?
answer_data: Result section listing suppressed edges with their justification codes
Prohibition on removing suppressed edges from the traversal record
Counts reported separately for traversed, suppressed and unmatched edges

data_elements.name: Exclusion identifier
data_elements.description: Addressable identifier of the exclusion statement.

data_elements.name: Exclusion scope
data_elements.description: The edge, relation-type class, subgraph or neighbourhood over which the exclusion applies, plus the impact question class it applies to.

data_elements.name: Exclusion justification code
data_elements.description: Governed code stating why propagation is withheld despite the edge being present.

data_elements.name: Exclusion expiry
data_elements.description: Timestamp after which the exclusion no longer applies and the edge returns to normal licensing.

data_elements.name: Exclusion evidence reference
data_elements.description: References to the evidence and the approval record supporting the exclusion.

artifacts.name: Propagation exclusion statement
artifacts.description: A standalone, addressable statement that a present edge or edge class is suppressed for a named impact question, carrying justification code, scope, effective and expiry times, evidence references and approver. Kept separate from the edge record so the underlying fact is never mutated by a policy decision.
media_or_form: standalone statement record, format-neutral
projection to a VEX-style justification document
annotation attached to a released projection's suppressed-edge section
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system identifier where an upstream exception or exploitability system issues one; otherwise a governed IRI; otherwise a Dimension-minted UUID or ULID. The referenced edge key is carried as a foreign reference, never as the exclusion's own identity.

layers.name: Completeness and closed-world declaration
layers.description: The declarations that must exist before any statement about absence, non-reachability or 'no impact' may be published, including the enumeration frontier actually covered and the gaps declared as known unknowns.

findings.name: Completeness declaration and enumeration frontier
findings.description: Absence of an edge is not evidence of absence of dependency. CycloneDX states plainly that objects not represented in the dependency graph may have unknown dependencies and that implementations should treat this as opaque rather than as dependency-freedom; RDF is a purely assertional language with no way to express absence; SPDX therefore carries an explicit three-valued completeness marker on the relationship itself. This finding requires a scoped completeness declaration naming the node scope, relation types and traversal depth actually enumerated, the gaps recorded as known unknowns, and the flag that licenses a closed-world reading. Any negative conclusion must cite a resolvable declaration that covers the queried scope.

questions.text: Is the enumerated edge set for this scope complete, incomplete, or is no assertion made?
answer_data: Three-valued completeness code aligned to SPDX complete, incomplete and noAssertion
Basis for the claim, such as an exhaustive manifest parse or a partial scan
Default of noAssertion when nothing has been declared

questions.text: Which node scope, relation types and traversal depth does the completeness declaration actually cover?
answer_data: Node or subgraph scope the declaration applies to
Relation type codes enumerated and those explicitly not enumerated
Maximum traversal depth reached and whether the frontier was truncated

questions.text: Which gaps are declared as known unknowns rather than treated as absent edges?
answer_data: Enumerated gap records naming the node or edge class that could not be resolved
Reason for each gap, such as an opaque binary, a closed upstream or an unresolvable reference
Distinguished no-assertion marker separate from a positive assertion that nothing exists

questions.text: What licenses a closed-world reading so that absence of an edge may be read as absence of dependency?
answer_data: Explicit closed-world flag scoped to the declared frontier, defaulting to false
Named authority that may set the flag and the evidence required
Rule that a negative conclusion outside the declared frontier is invalid regardless of the flag

questions.text: How long does a completeness declaration remain valid, and what invalidates it?
answer_data: Declared validity interval with RFC 3339 bounds
Invalidation triggers such as a new edge assertion inside the scope or a superseded endpoint
Re-declaration obligation and the owning role

data_elements.name: Completeness declaration identifier
data_elements.description: Addressable identifier of the declaration, citable from any negative conclusion.

data_elements.name: Completeness value
data_elements.description: Three-valued marker: complete, incomplete or noAssertion.

data_elements.name: Enumeration frontier
data_elements.description: Node scope, relation types covered and maximum depth actually enumerated, with a truncation indicator.

data_elements.name: Known unknown record
data_elements.description: Declared gap in enumeration, with the affected node or edge class and the reason it could not be resolved.

data_elements.name: Closed-world flag
data_elements.description: Whether absence within the declared frontier may be read as absence in reality; defaults to false.

artifacts.name: Completeness declaration
artifacts.description: A scoped, time-bounded declaration of how exhaustively an edge set was enumerated, naming the frontier, the completeness value, the declared known unknowns and the closed-world flag, signed by the declaring role. Cited by identifier from every projection that makes a negative or reachability claim.
media_or_form: scoped declaration record, format-neutral
projection to an SPDX relationship completeness value plus a scope note
header block attached to a released impact projection
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed identifier issued by the declaring owner package; date-free and stable across re-declaration, with each re-declaration recorded as a new version that supersedes the prior one by explicit pointer.

bundles.name: Derived graph projections and result semantics
bundles.description: Everything computed rather than asserted: the run descriptor that makes a derived result reproducible and falsifiable, and the declared semantics of each result type - paths, cycles and strongly connected groups, reachability, fan-in and fan-out, cut sets and alternative paths.
bundles.rationale: A graph result is meaningless without its algorithm, parameters, edge filter and input snapshot: implementation documentation for strongly connected components shows results reflect a projected graph at execution time, and ISO/IEC 39075 shows that even 'a path' is ambiguous until a restrictor such as walk, trail, acyclic or simple is fixed. IEC 61025 and IEC 61078 supply the established qualitative vocabulary for cut sets and success paths, but bind those results to a stated method and stated assumptions. Separating this bundle from the fact base enforces the rule that projections are never merged into the asserted edge set and are re-derived rather than patched.

layers.name: Analysis run and projection provenance
layers.description: How a derived result is bound to the algorithm, parameters, edge filter and immutable input snapshot that produced it, and how it becomes stale.

findings.name: Declared analysis run over a named snapshot
findings.description: A derived result is admissible only as a projection carrying: the algorithm identifier and version, the full parameter set, the edge-selection filter (relation types, licence profile, modality inclusions, exclusions applied, temporal reference), the digest of the immutable input edge set, the run execution time, a determinism class and any supersession pointer. This mirrors how graph analytics actually behave, computing over a projected in-memory graph whose results reflect that projection at execution time. The model records the run; it never executes it, and it holds no claim over the evaluator's own execution logs or audit records.

questions.text: Which algorithm identifier and version produced this derived result?
answer_data: Registered method identifier with version, distinct per algorithm variant
Implementation or evaluator reference where the same method has several implementations
Rule that an algorithm change requires a new method identifier rather than a silent revision

questions.text: Which parameters, edge filters and modality inclusions defined the analysed subgraph?
answer_data: Complete parameter set including seeds, depth bounds and direction
Edge filter naming relation types, licence profile version and applied exclusions
Which relation modalities were admitted, in particular whether hypothetical edges were included

questions.text: Against which immutable snapshot of the asserted edge set was the run executed?
answer_data: Snapshot digest over the canonicalised selected edge set
Reference to the completeness declarations covering the snapshot scope
Temporal reference instant the snapshot represents, separate from the run execution time

questions.text: Is the result reproducible from the recorded snapshot and parameters, and where is it not?
answer_data: Determinism class such as deterministic, tie-break dependent or randomised with seed
Recorded random seed or tie-break rule where applicable
Known non-determinism such as arbitrary representative selection within a component

questions.text: What makes a stored projection stale, and how is supersession recorded?
answer_data: Staleness triggers: input snapshot digest mismatch, licence profile revision, completeness re-declaration
Supersedes and superseded-by pointers between run descriptors
Rule that a stale projection may not support a negative or absence conclusion

data_elements.name: Analysis method identifier
data_elements.description: Registered identifier and version of the algorithm that produced the result.

data_elements.name: Method parameters
data_elements.description: Complete parameter set including seeds, bounds, direction and tie-break or random seed.

data_elements.name: Edge selection filter
data_elements.description: Relation types, licence profile version, applied exclusions, admitted modalities and temporal reference that defined the analysed subgraph.

data_elements.name: Input snapshot digest
data_elements.description: Content digest over the canonicalised selected edge set, giving the projection a falsifiable input identity.

data_elements.name: Run execution time
data_elements.description: When the analysis was executed, recorded separately from edge validity time and from the snapshot reference instant.

data_elements.name: Determinism class
data_elements.description: Whether the result is fully deterministic, tie-break dependent or seeded-random.

data_elements.name: Supersession reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the run descriptor this projection replaces, or to the one that replaced it.

artifacts.name: Analysis run descriptor
artifacts.description: The header record that makes every derived result reproducible and challengeable: method identity and version, parameters, edge filter, snapshot digest, cited completeness declarations, run time, determinism class and supersession pointers. Every result set in this bundle is invalid without a resolvable descriptor.
media_or_form: run descriptor record, format-neutral
manifest header prepended to any released result set
provenance-style record projectable to a PROV activity description without importing PROV lifecycle semantics
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed method identifier plus input snapshot digest plus a zero-padded monotonic run ordinal scoped to that method and snapshot; where an external evaluator issues its own authoritative run identifier, that master-system identifier takes precedence and the composite key is retained as a secondary key.

layers.name: Result-type semantics
layers.description: The declared meaning of each derived result class: path results and their restrictors, cycles and strongly connected groups, and reachability with the criticality measures built on it.

findings.name: Path results, path restrictors and alternative paths
findings.description: A path result is uninterpretable until its restrictor is declared. ISO/IEC 39075 fixes the distinctions normatively with walk, trail, acyclic and simple restrictors controlling whether nodes or edges may repeat, alongside match modes and path search. A path result must therefore state its restrictor, direction, depth or hop bound and what happened at that bound, and whether it claims all paths, shortest paths, k paths or a single witness. Alternative-path counts are only meaningful with a declared disjointness criterion, which is the success-path dual of the cut-set view in reliability modelling.

questions.text: Which path restrictor governs the result: walk, trail, acyclic or simple?
answer_data: Restrictor code aligned to the GQL path restrictor vocabulary
Statement of whether repeated nodes and repeated edges are permitted
Default restrictor when the consumer does not specify one

questions.text: What depth or hop bound and traversal direction were applied, and what happened at the bound?
answer_data: Maximum hop or depth bound and traversal direction
Truncation indicator distinguishing exhausted search from bound-limited search
Count of frontier nodes left unexpanded at the bound

questions.text: Does the result claim all paths, shortest paths, k paths, or a single witness path?
answer_data: Selection mode code and, for k paths, the value of k
Cost or weight function used for shortest-path selection, if any
Explicit statement that a witness path does not imply the absence of others

questions.text: How many node-disjoint or edge-disjoint alternative paths exist between the two endpoints?
answer_data: Disjointness criterion applied (node-disjoint, edge-disjoint or none)
Count of alternative paths found and whether the search was exhaustive
Reference to the method used, since alternative-path counting is method-sensitive

questions.text: How is an individual path addressed and compared across runs?
answer_data: Ordered edge-key sequence as the path's natural key
Digest over that sequence for compact addressing
Comparison rule when a path is stable but its constituent edges have been superseded

data_elements.name: Path restrictor
data_elements.description: Declared restrictor: walk, trail, acyclic or simple.

data_elements.name: Depth or hop bound
data_elements.description: Maximum traversal depth applied, with a truncation indicator.

data_elements.name: Path selection mode
data_elements.description: Whether the result claims all, shortest, k-shortest or any single path.

data_elements.name: Path edge sequence
data_elements.description: Ordered sequence of edge keys constituting the path, serving as its natural key.

data_elements.name: Alternative-path disjointness criterion
data_elements.description: Node-disjoint, edge-disjoint or none, governing how alternative paths were counted.

artifacts.name: Path result set
artifacts.description: The enumerated paths returned by one analysis run, each with its ordered edge sequence and digest, bound to the run descriptor and carrying the restrictor, bound, selection mode, truncation state and disjointness criterion that define what the set claims.
media_or_form: result set record, format-neutral
ordered edge-key sequences with per-path digests
projection to a GQL path result or a property-graph path object
artifacts.identity_strategy: Analysis run descriptor identifier plus a zero-padded ordinal for the result set, with each path addressed by the digest of its ordered edge-key sequence; no date component in any identifier.

findings.name: Cycles, strongly connected groups and closure safety
findings.description: Directed dependency graphs are not reliably acyclic. A strongly connected component is a maximal set of nodes with a directed path between every pair, and its presence changes what may be claimed: unbounded transitive closure over a cycle does not terminate, topological ordering is undefined inside a component, and shortest-path depth claims must state their restrictor. This finding records component membership, cycle witnesses, the acyclic condensation where computed, and an explicit closure-safety marker stating whether transitive or ordering claims over the analysed subgraph are sound.

questions.text: Does the analysed subgraph contain directed cycles, and which edges witness them?
answer_data: Boolean cyclicity result for the analysed subgraph under the declared edge filter
One or more witness cycles as ordered edge-key sequences
Whether cycle enumeration was exhaustive or bounded

questions.text: Which nodes form strongly connected groups, and how is each group addressed?
answer_data: Component assignment mapping each node to a component identifier
Component identity strategy independent of any arbitrarily chosen representative node
Component size distribution and the count of non-trivial components

questions.text: How do detected cycles constrain transitive closure, ordering and depth claims?
answer_data: Closure-safety marker stating whether unbounded transitive claims are sound
Mandatory depth bound or component-collapse strategy where cycles are present
Explicit statement that topological ordering is undefined within a non-trivial component

questions.text: Is the acyclic condensation of the graph recorded, and how does it relate to the original asserted edges?
answer_data: Reference to the condensation projection and its own run descriptor
Mapping from each condensation node back to its member node set
Rule that condensation edges are derived, never asserted, and carry derived modality

data_elements.name: Component identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of a strongly connected group, assigned so it does not depend on an arbitrary representative node.

data_elements.name: Component membership
data_elements.description: Mapping of node references to component identifiers for the analysed subgraph.

data_elements.name: Cycle witness
data_elements.description: Ordered edge-key sequence demonstrating a directed cycle.

data_elements.name: Condensation reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the acyclic condensation projection derived from the component assignment.

data_elements.name: Closure safety marker
data_elements.description: Whether transitive closure and ordering claims over the analysed subgraph are sound given detected cycles and declared bounds.

artifacts.name: Component and cycle result set
artifacts.description: The component assignment produced by one run, with cycle witnesses, component size statistics, the closure-safety marker and an optional condensation reference, bound to its run descriptor and snapshot digest.
media_or_form: result set record, format-neutral
node-to-component assignment table
derived condensation graph projection referenced by identifier
artifacts.identity_strategy: Analysis run descriptor identifier plus a zero-padded result ordinal; component identifiers are minted per run as ULIDs and mapped to their member sets, so component identity is never silently reused across snapshots.

findings.name: Reachability, negative claims, fan-in, fan-out and cut sets
findings.description: The impact answer itself: the set reachable from a seed under the declared licence, modality and temporal filters, together with the structural measures built on that traversal - fan-in and fan-out degree, minimal cut sets whose removal disconnects a seed from a target, and the count of surviving alternative paths. Fault tree analysis supplies the cut-set vocabulary and the discipline of identifying assumptions and event boundaries explicitly; reliability block diagrams supply the dual success-path view. The controlling rule is asymmetric: a positive reachability claim needs only the traversal record, while any negative claim - not reachable, not impacted, no dependency - additionally requires a resolvable completeness declaration with the closed-world flag covering the queried scope.

questions.text: Which nodes are reachable from the seed under the declared licence, modality and temporal filters?
answer_data: Reachable node set with, for each node, at least one witness path or hop distance
The seed set and traversal direction that produced it
Counts of edges traversed, suppressed by exclusion and unmatched by any licence profile

questions.text: On what basis may this result state that a node is not reachable or not impacted?
answer_data: Identifier of the completeness declaration covering the queried scope, with its closed-world flag set
Explicit downgrade to 'not known to be reachable' where the declaration is absent, incomplete or stale
Record of which known unknowns bound the strength of the claim

questions.text: What are the fan-in and fan-out degrees of the node, and over which edge selection were they counted?
answer_data: In-degree and out-degree counts with the edge filter and licence profile they were computed under
Whether multi-edges, self-loops and suppressed edges were counted or excluded
Whether the count is over asserted edges only or includes derived edges

questions.text: Which minimal sets of nodes or edges, if removed, disconnect the seed from the target?
answer_data: Enumerated minimal cut sets with their cardinality, and identification of any single points of failure
Whether enumeration was exhaustive or bounded, and the bound applied
Method reference and the stated assumptions and event boundaries of the analysis

questions.text: How is a what-if impact answer over hypothetical or removed edges kept separate from the actual-state answer?
answer_data: Scenario identifier and the edge additions or removals it applies
Mandatory labelling of the result as hypothetical, including in any downstream export
Prohibition on citing a hypothetical result as evidence of the actual state

data_elements.name: Reachability set
data_elements.description: Nodes reachable from the seed under the declared filters, each with a witness path or hop distance.

data_elements.name: Negative claim marker
data_elements.description: Whether the result asserts non-reachability, and the identifier of the completeness declaration that licenses it.

data_elements.name: Fan-in degree
data_elements.description: Count of licensed incoming edges at a node under the declared edge filter.

data_elements.name: Fan-out degree
data_elements.description: Count of licensed outgoing edges at a node under the declared edge filter.

data_elements.name: Cut set
data_elements.description: A minimal set of nodes or edges whose removal disconnects the seed from the target, with cardinality and exhaustiveness marker.

data_elements.name: Surviving alternative path count
data_elements.description: Number of disjoint alternative paths remaining between seed and target under the declared disjointness criterion.

artifacts.name: Impact and criticality result set
artifacts.description: The released impact answer for one run: reachability set with witness paths, suppressed and unmatched edge counts, fan-in and fan-out measures, enumerated cut sets and surviving alternative-path counts, with every negative claim carrying an inline reference to the completeness declaration that licenses it and every hypothetical component labelled as such.
media_or_form: result set record, format-neutral
impact report with a mandatory completeness and assumptions header
criticality measure table keyed by node reference
artifacts.identity_strategy: Analysis run descriptor identifier plus a zero-padded result ordinal; node and edge entries are addressed by the endpoint references and edge keys owned by the fact base, never by report-local sequence numbers.

functions.name: Assert dependency edge
functions.description: Record a new asserted dependency edge as an immutable primary fact with typed direction, lifecycle scope, validity window, provenance and confidence.
inputs: Source and target endpoint references resolvable in the owning inventory model
Relation type code from a governed vocabulary
Lifecycle scope codes, validity window, asserting agent, evidence references and confidence
outputs: Edge assertion record with an assigned identifier under the identity priority rule
Rejection with reason where an endpoint reference does not resolve
preconditions: Endpoint references resolve, or the caller explicitly quarantines the edge as unresolved
Relation type code exists in a bound vocabulary version
Validity and assertion timestamps supplied as RFC 3339 values with an explicit offset or Z
effects: Creates one immutable edge assertion record in this model's fact base
Invalidates by digest mismatch any projection whose input snapshot included the affected scope
Does not create, modify or classify the endpoint entities, which remain owned by the inventory model

functions.name: Classify relation modality
functions.description: Assign exactly one modality (direct, transitive, inferred, hypothetical) to a dependency statement and attach the derivation basis for non-direct modalities.
inputs: Dependency statement reference
Proposed modality and, where applicable, the property characteristic, property chain, rule or closure method reference with premise edge keys
outputs: Modality assignment with derivation basis and materialisation flag
Validation error when a non-direct modality is proposed without a resolvable basis
preconditions: Any declared transitive property or property chain is resolvable and its global-restriction status is recorded
Premise edges cited by a transitive statement are resolvable and within their validity window
effects: Sets the modality discriminator carried on the statement
Blocks promotion of a derived statement to direct modality without a new agent assertion
Does not perform entailment or invoke a reasoner; entailment computation remains with the external reasoner

functions.name: Declare propagation licence profile
functions.description: Publish or revise a versioned profile stating which relation types, lifecycle scopes, directions, temporal overlaps and confidence thresholds permit impact to traverse an edge for a named class of impact question.
inputs: Impact question class the profile serves
Relation type codes, permitted directions, lifecycle scopes, temporal overlap predicate and confidence threshold
Precedence rank and approving role
outputs: Change classification indicating whether the revision is breaking for existing projections
preconditions: Approving role holds authority over the profile's owner package
Deny-by-default is stated explicitly and no implicit fallback is introduced
effects: Creates a new profile version; prior versions remain resolvable so historical projections stay interpretable
Marks projections computed under a superseded profile version as requiring re-derivation
Does not enforce traversal at query time; enforcement is performed by the consuming evaluator

functions.name: Record propagation exclusion
functions.description: Record a typed, scoped and expiring statement that a present edge or edge class does not propagate impact for a stated and evidenced reason.
inputs: Target edge, relation-type class or subgraph, and the impact question class affected
Justification code from the governed exclusion vocabulary
Evidence references, reviewing role, effective-from and expiry timestamps
outputs: Exclusion statement artifact linked to the affected edges by reference
Rejection where no justification code is supplied
preconditions: A justification code is present; free text alone is invalid
Effective and expiry times are RFC 3339 values with an explicit offset or Z
effects: Creates an exclusion statement without mutating the underlying edge assertion
Requires downstream results to report the edge as suppressed rather than absent
Does not adjudicate the underlying vulnerability or exception; that remains with the referenced exception model

functions.name: Declare completeness and enumeration frontier
functions.description: Publish a scoped, time-bounded declaration of how exhaustively an edge set was enumerated, including declared known unknowns and the closed-world flag.
inputs: Node or subgraph scope, relation types enumerated and traversal depth reached
Completeness value (complete, incomplete, noAssertion) and its basis
Known-unknown records, validity interval and declaring role
outputs: Completeness declaration artifact citable by identifier from any projection
Default noAssertion result where the declarant cannot substantiate exhaustiveness
preconditions: The declaring role is authorised to set the closed-world flag for the named scope
Each known unknown names the affected node or edge class and the reason it is unresolved
effects: Creates a declaration version and supersedes any prior version by explicit pointer
Licenses negative conclusions only within the declared frontier and validity interval
Does not itself close the world for any scope it does not name

functions.name: Register analysis projection
functions.description: Record a derived graph result produced by an external evaluator as a projection, binding it to method identity and version, parameters, edge filter, input snapshot digest, run time and determinism class.
inputs: Registered method identifier and version, plus the full parameter set
Edge selection filter including licence profile version, admitted modalities, applied exclusions and temporal reference
Input snapshot digest, cited completeness declarations, run execution time and the result payload
outputs: Analysis run descriptor plus the associated result set artifact
Rejection where the method identifier is unregistered or the snapshot digest does not resolve
preconditions: The input snapshot digest resolves to a canonicalised, retained edge set
Cited completeness declarations are current for the analysed scope
Result semantics are declared: path restrictor, bounds, selection mode or component identity strategy as applicable
effects: Creates an immutable projection record separate from the asserted edge set
Never merges derived statements into the fact base
Does not execute the algorithm and asserts no ownership of the evaluator's execution logs or audit records

functions.name: Validate absence or non-reachability claim
functions.description: Check that a proposed negative claim - not reachable, not impacted, no dependency - cites a resolvable, current completeness declaration whose frontier covers the queried scope, and return a verdict.
inputs: Proposed negative claim with its queried scope and seed set
Referenced projection and its run descriptor
Referenced completeness declaration identifier
outputs: Verdict of licensed, downgraded or rejected, with the failing condition named
Rewritten claim strength, for example 'not known to be reachable', where the declaration is absent, partial or stale
preconditions: The projection's snapshot digest still resolves and the projection is not superseded
The completeness declaration is within its validity interval and its closed-world flag covers the queried scope
effects: Produces a validation verdict over this model's own records
Prevents publication of an unsupported negative conclusion by downgrading its stated strength
Does not enforce access, block delivery or write an audit record; enforcement and audit remain with the consuming service and the Dimension's audit model

functions.name: Supersede stale projection
functions.description: Mark a stored projection as stale and record its supersession when its input snapshot, licence profile version or completeness declaration has changed.
inputs: Projection or run descriptor reference
Staleness trigger: snapshot digest mismatch, licence profile revision or completeness re-declaration
Replacement run descriptor reference where one exists
outputs: Updated run descriptor carrying a staleness marker and supersession pointers
List of downstream results that inherited the staleness
preconditions: The triggering change is itself recorded and resolvable
The projection has not already been tombstoned
effects: Marks the projection stale and forbids its use as support for a negative or absence conclusion
Propagates the staleness marker to derived results that consumed it
Does not delete the projection or trigger re-computation; re-derivation is requested from the external evaluator

composition.target: Component, asset or subject inventory model (SPDX 3.0.1 and CycloneDX 1.6 aligned)
composition.purpose: Edge endpoints are carried only as resolvable references. Identity, versioning, classification and inventory completeness of the depended-on subjects stay with the inventory model; this model carries the reference, the resolution scheme binding and the failure behaviour when a reference does not resolve, and reproduces none of the inventory's lifecycle or curation functions.

Align assertion provenance and derivation vocabulary for edges and projections so they are exportable as PROV descriptions. The alignment is deliberately partial: PROV's non-transitivity of derivation is honoured as a constraint, while PROV's activity, agent and delegation lifecycle is not imported.

Bind the declared path restrictor and selection mode on a path result to the standard's walk, trail, acyclic and simple vocabulary so results are interpretable across engines. Query syntax, evaluation and execution planning remain in the engine.

Reference a declared transitive property or object property chain as the derivation basis for an inferred edge, including whether the OWL 2 global restrictions on composite properties are satisfied. Entailment computation and reasoner materialisation stay outside.

composition.target: Reliability and risk analysis model (IEC 61025 fault tree analysis and IEC 61078 reliability block diagrams aligned)
composition.purpose: Cut-set and success-path results are recorded here as method-declared projections with their stated assumptions and event boundaries. Probability quantification, importance factors, risk acceptance and dependability verdicts belong to the risk model and are referenced, not reproduced.

composition.target: Exception and exploitability statement model (VEX / OpenVEX aligned)
composition.purpose: A propagation exclusion may cite an external exploitability or exception statement as its evidence and may carry the justification code and its scope binding. Vulnerability status determination, remediation and disclosure remain with that model.

The immutable input snapshot that gives a projection its falsifiable identity is composed from a shared snapshot and digest facility: canonicalisation, content digest and retention of the selected edge set. This model supplies the edge-set selection and consumes the digest as the snapshot's identifier.
Edge validity windows, exclusion effective and expiry times and completeness declaration intervals reuse the shared validity-period mixin rather than redefining interval semantics locally.

composition.target: Change, release and remediation execution model
composition.purpose: An impact projection is delivered as an input to change planning, carrying its completeness declaration and assumptions. Deciding, approving, scheduling and executing a change, and recording that execution, belong entirely to the change model.

composition.target: Host subject model applying this mixin
composition.purpose: The mixin specialises only the dependency and impact surface of its host subject: edge typing bound to the host's vocabulary and licence profiles written for the host's impact questions. Generic identity, authority, record lifecycle and conflict resolution remain with the host and are not duplicated here.

owner_package_requirements: Name a single owner package for the dependency-edge namespace, the exclusion justification vocabulary and the propagation licence profiles, with a named approving role for each profile version.

Maintain a registry of analysis method identifiers and versions; an algorithm change requires a new method identifier rather than a silent revision, and each entry names the evaluator implementations that may claim it.
Publish and re-publish completeness declarations for every scope over which the Dimension permits negative or non-reachability conclusions, and name the role authorised to set the closed-world flag.
Record, for every projection, which external evaluator produced it; the owner package must not claim ownership of that evaluator's execution, enforcement or audit records.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Relation type codes, exclusion justification codes and analysis method identifiers are IRIs or governed codes in a namespace owned by the adopting Dimension, with explicit binding statements to external vocabularies (SPDX RelationshipType, SPDX LifecycleScopeType, CycloneDX dependsOn and provides, OpenVEX justifications, GQL path restrictors). Bindings are recorded as alignments with a vocabulary version, never as claims of conformance. Local identifiers are lower-kebab-case and carry no date component.
registry_links: Vercy registry entry vr.wm-xct-037 (WM-XCT-037 Dependency / Impact), nav path NAV.XCT.DEP
SPDX 3.0.1 Core vocabularies for RelationshipType, RelationshipCompleteness and LifecycleScopeType
ISO/IEC 39075:2024 GQL for path restrictor and match-mode terminology
OpenVEX justification vocabulary for exclusion codes

canonicalization_rules: The canonical natural key of an asserted edge is the ordered tuple of source reference, relation type, sorted target reference set, sorted lifecycle scope set and validity start; target and scope sets are sorted by their governed identifier to make the key stable under reordering.
All timestamps are normalised to RFC 3339 with whole-second or finer precision and an explicit numeric offset or Z before any digest is computed.

A snapshot digest is computed over the canonicalised, key-sorted selected edge set together with the edge filter and the identifiers of the cited completeness declarations, so that a filter change yields a different snapshot identity.

Canonicalisation is defined over the abstract record, not over any serialisation; JSON, YAML, RDF, Markdown, property-graph and document-store forms must all produce the same canonical key and digest.
patch_rules: Asserted edges are append-only. A correction is a new assertion carrying a supersedes pointer and a correction reason; in-place mutation of an edge record is prohibited.
Derived projections are never patched. A changed input produces a new run descriptor and a new result set; the prior projection is marked stale and superseded.
Propagation licence profiles and completeness declarations are versioned artifacts; a revision creates a new version and retains the prior version as resolvable.
An exclusion statement is amended only by issuing a superseding statement; expiry lapse is recorded, not backdated.
compatibility_rules: Adding a relation type code, a path restrictor binding or a new analysis method identifier is a minor, backward-compatible change.
Changing a propagation licence profile from deny to allow for any relation type or lifecycle scope is a breaking change and invalidates projections computed under the prior version.
Withdrawing, narrowing or expiring a completeness declaration is a breaking change for every negative conclusion that cited it; those conclusions must be re-validated or downgraded.
Changing the canonical edge key composition, the digest algorithm or the modality vocabulary is a breaking change requiring a model version increment and re-derivation of affected projections.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier: the identifier issued by the system of record that asserts the edge or governs its endpoints - for example an SPDX Element identifier, a CycloneDX bom-ref within the owning inventory, or an external evaluator's own run identifier for a projection.

Governed global identifier or IRI from a published namespace where no master-system identifier exists - for example a purl, a CPE or a Dimension-owned IRI for a licence profile, completeness declaration or analysis method.
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, recorded together with its minting authority and the natural key it stands for.

A date, a version label, a file path or a report sequence number is never an identifier; the canonical edge key and the path edge-sequence digest are natural keys retained for deduplication and comparison, not substitutes for an assigned identifier.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values use RFC 3339 date-time with at least whole seconds and an explicit numeric UTC offset or Z; local times without an offset are rejected. Edge validity time (the interval over which the dependency is claimed to hold), assertion or observation time (when the claim was recorded), and analysis-run execution or ingestion time (when a projection was computed and when it was registered) are stored as separate fields and are never conflated, because a projection is normally computed after the edge state it describes and may be ingested later still.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts are the repeatable outputs of analysis: run descriptors and result sets. Each is named by its analysis method identifier, its input snapshot digest and a zero-padded monotonic run ordinal scoped to that method-and-snapshot pair. Ordinals are never reused or renumbered, gaps are permitted and meaningful (they record a withdrawn run), and no ordinal encodes a date.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every result-set artifact carries its own content digest plus the digest of its input edge set and the identifiers of the cited completeness declarations and licence profile versions. A projection whose input digest no longer resolves, or whose cited declaration has been superseded or has expired, is marked stale and must not be used to support any negative, non-reachability or 'no impact' conclusion; positive traversal witnesses from a stale projection may still be cited if labelled with the snapshot they came from.

policies: No absence, non-reachability or 'no impact' conclusion may be published without a resolvable, current completeness declaration whose frontier covers the queried scope and whose closed-world flag is set; otherwise the claim is downgraded to 'not known to be reachable'.

Derived results are projections and are never merged into the asserted edge set; asserted and derived statements remain separately addressable and separately queryable at every layer, in every storage form.

Propagation is deny-by-default: an edge licenses impact traversal only when an explicit licence profile matches it, and edges matched by no profile are reported as a distinct unmatched category rather than dropped.

An edge suppressed by an exclusion must be reported as suppressed with its justification code; rendering a suppressed edge as absent is prohibited because absence carries a completeness claim that an exclusion does not make.
Hypothetical edges and scenarios are excluded from actual-state answers by default; any answer that consumed them is labelled hypothetical, and that label survives export.

This model records analysis declarations only. It does not execute algorithms, enforce access, schedule or perform change, or generate audit trails; those remain with the referenced evaluator, enforcement point, change model and the adopting Dimension's audit service.

read: Every read of an edge returns its modality, validity window and assertion provenance; a consumer must never receive a bare endpoint pair.
Every read of a projection returns its run descriptor: method identifier and version, parameters, edge filter, snapshot digest and cited completeness declarations.
A read that would answer a negative or absence question returns the governing completeness declaration alongside the answer, or returns the downgraded claim strength.
Stale projections remain readable but are returned with an explicit staleness marker and the trigger that caused it.
create: An edge assertion is created only with resolvable endpoint references, a governed relation type, a declared modality and assertion provenance; unresolved endpoints are quarantined rather than silently accepted.

A projection is created only with a registered method identifier and version, a resolvable snapshot digest and a declared result semantics (path restrictor and selection mode, or component identity strategy, as applicable).
An exclusion is created only with a governed justification code, an applicability scope and an effective interval.
A completeness declaration is created only by a role authorised for the named scope, and defaults to noAssertion where exhaustiveness cannot be substantiated.
update: Asserted edges are immutable; change is expressed only by a superseding assertion carrying a reason and a supersedes pointer.
Projections are never updated in place; a changed input produces a new run descriptor and result set and marks the prior one superseded.
Licence profiles, exclusions and completeness declarations are updated by issuing a new version that retains the prior version as resolvable.
Modality may never be upgraded from a derived value to direct without a new agent assertion recorded as its own edge fact.
delete: This model's own records are tombstoned, not erased. A retired edge assertion, exclusion, completeness declaration or projection retains its identifier, canonical key, modality, validity window, supersession pointer and retirement reason for the retention period set by the adopting Dimension, so that historical projections remain explainable.

A tombstoned edge is never counted as an absence: any traversal or negative claim that encounters a tombstone must treat it as a declared known unknown unless a current completeness declaration covers the scope.

Deletion is cascade-safe in one direction only: retiring an edge marks dependent projections stale but never deletes them; retiring a completeness declaration invalidates the negative conclusions that cited it and requires their re-validation.

Physical erasure, cryptographic shredding, legal hold and jurisdictional erasure requests are executed by the adopting Dimension's records-retention policy together with the referenced storage and inventory models; this model owns only the disposition marker, the tombstone content rule and the prohibition on reading a tombstone as absence. Where an erasure obligation conflicts with the tombstone rule, the Dimension's retention policy prevails and the resulting gap must be recorded as a declared known unknown.

roles.name: Edge assertion steward
responsibilities: Records and supersedes asserted edges, ensuring endpoint references resolve and provenance and confidence are populated
Quarantines unresolved or conflicting assertions rather than dropping them
Maintains the binding between local relation type codes and external vocabulary versions

roles.name: Propagation policy owner
responsibilities: Authors, versions and approves propagation licence profiles per impact question class
Sets and reviews confidence thresholds and precedence ranks, and classifies revisions as breaking or minor
Reviews and approves propagation exclusions and their justification codes and expiry

roles.name: Completeness declarant
responsibilities: Declares the enumeration frontier, completeness value and known unknowns for a named scope
Holds the sole authority to set the closed-world flag and to re-declare or withdraw a declaration
Triggers re-validation of negative conclusions when a declaration lapses or narrows

roles.name: Analysis method registrar
responsibilities: Registers analysis method identifiers and versions and the evaluator implementations permitted to claim them
Verifies that registered projections carry complete parameters, edge filter, snapshot digest and determinism class
Marks projections stale on snapshot, profile or declaration change and records supersession

roles.name: Impact analyst and projection consumer
responsibilities: Requests projections with an explicit question class, seed set, temporal reference and licence profile
Publishes impact answers only with their completeness declaration, assumptions and suppressed-edge counts attached
Labels every hypothetical or scenario-based answer and does not cite it as evidence of actual state

access.default_rule: Least privilege with inherited sensitivity: a derived projection inherits the most restrictive classification of any contributing edge, endpoint reference, exclusion evidence item or completeness declaration in its input snapshot. A caller who may not read a contributing edge may not read a projection that reveals it, including indirectly through a witness path.
exceptions: Aggregate-only release: fan-in, fan-out, component sizes and cut-set cardinalities may be released with endpoint references redacted, provided witness paths are withheld and the redaction is stated in the result.

Incident triage break-glass: time-boxed read of reachability answers for a named seed, granted by the propagation policy owner, requiring the completeness declaration to be attached and the grant to expire automatically.
Supply-chain disclosure: an edge set may be released to an external party under the completeness value and known unknowns of its declaration, never as a bare list that implies exhaustiveness.
Hypothetical scenario sandbox: scenario edge sets are readable only within the scenario scope and are never returned by an actual-state query.
audit_requirements: Every released projection carries its method identifier and version, snapshot digest, licence profile version and cited completeness declaration identifiers so that an external audit record can be correlated to it.
Every negative or absence conclusion records which completeness declaration licensed it and which known unknowns bounded it.
Break-glass and aggregate-only releases record the granting role, the scope, the expiry and the redaction applied.

Access events and the audit trail itself are generated and retained by the adopting Dimension's audit service; this model supplies correlation metadata only and asserts no ownership of audit-record semantics or retention.

read_order: AGENTS.md - resolve Name, Type, Registry ID and the four URL fields before any other action
Specification URL - read the model scope, boundary notes and out-of-scope list to confirm the request belongs to this model
Completeness declaration URL - resolve the declaration covering the queried scope before formulating any absence, non-reachability or 'no impact' answer
Propagation licence profile URL - resolve the governing profile version before traversing any edge
Analysis method registry URL - resolve the method identifier and version before registering or interpreting a projection
Storage type URL and Interface URL - bind the abstract records to the concrete storage and access projection in use
