Processes URL - follow the assertion, declaration, registration, validation and supersession procedures

coverage.claim: This pass covers the graph-analysis semantics of WM-XCT-037: asserted edges as immutable primary facts, modality discrimination across direct, transitive, inferred and hypothetical relations, deny-by-default propagation licensing with typed exclusions, mandatory completeness and closed-world declarations before any absence or non-reachability claim, and derived results (paths and path restrictors, cycles and strongly connected groups, reachability, fan-in and fan-out, cut sets and alternative paths) recorded as snapshot-bound projections with declared algorithm and parameters. Structural nodes are grounded in SPDX 3.0.1 relationship and completeness semantics, CycloneDX's explicit opaque-absence rule, W3C PROV-CONSTRAINTS and RDF 1.1 Semantics on non-transitivity and non-obligatory materialisation, OWL 2 property characteristics, ISO/IEC 39075 path restrictors and IEC 61025 and 61078 cut-set and success-path vocabulary. It is not a graph database, a scheduler, a change executor or a risk quantification method, and it claims no conformance to any cited standard.

checklist.notes: Edge key, path edge-sequence digest, component identifier, run descriptor identity and declaration identifiers are all defined, with the identity priority placing the authoritative master-system identifier first and explicitly excluding dates, paths and report sequence numbers.

Edges are append-only with supersession; licence profiles, exclusions and completeness declarations are versioned; projections are re-derived and superseded rather than patched. Host-subject and endpoint-entity lifecycles are explicitly left to the host model and the inventory model.

The typed, directed, scoped edge is the core object; modality separates direct, transitive, inferred and hypothetical relations; composition links bind the model to inventory, provenance, GQL, OWL 2, reliability, VEX, snapshot, validity, change and host models with explicit ownership boundaries.

Edge validity window, assertion or observation time, snapshot reference instant, run execution time and ingestion time are separated; temporal overlap is a licensing condition; exclusions and completeness declarations expire. All times are RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z.

Every edge carries asserting agent, evidence and confidence; every projection carries method, parameters, edge filter, snapshot digest and cited declarations; derivation basis is mandatory for transitive and inferred statements. PROV is an alignment target, not an imported lifecycle.

Owner package requirements, five named roles and the composition ledger assign ownership; execution, enforcement, risk quantification, change execution and audit-trail generation are explicitly assigned elsewhere.

The absence-claim validation function returns licensed, downgraded or rejected verdicts; deny-by-default licensing, mandatory justification codes, closure-safety marking and determinism class are all checkable conditions. Validation produces verdicts, not enforcement.

Inherited-sensitivity default rule, four scopes, and four exception classes including aggregate-only release and time-boxed break-glass. Audit requirements are limited to correlation metadata the model must emit.

Tombstone rule with mandatory retained content, the prohibition on reading a tombstone as absence, one-directional cascade safety, and an explicit statement that physical erasure and legal hold are executed by the adopting Dimension's retention policy and the referenced storage and inventory models, with retention prevailing over the tombstone rule where they conflict.

Alignments declared to SPDX, CycloneDX, PROV, OWL 2, GQL, OpenVEX, IEC 61025 and IEC 61078, each as an alignment with a version binding rather than a conformance claim. Canonicalisation is defined over abstract records so all serialisations agree.

A dedicated layer and finding, grounded in the SPDX three-valued completeness vocabulary, the CycloneDX opaque-absence rule and RDF's purely assertional character; absence claims are structurally blocked without a covering declaration.

Cycle witnesses, strongly connected group membership, condensation and an explicit closure-safety marker constrain transitive, ordering and depth claims; unbounded closure over cyclic subgraphs is prohibited.

Fan-in, fan-out, cut-set cardinality, alternative-path counts and confidence are all defined with the edge selection they were computed under; counting rules for multi-edges, self-loops and suppressed edges are required to be stated.
Method identity and version, full parameters, snapshot digest, determinism class and recorded seeds or tie-break rules make each projection reproducible or explicitly flagged as non-reproducible.

checklist.dimension: security and privacy of the graph itself
checklist.notes: Inherited sensitivity and redaction exceptions are declared, but inference attacks that reconstruct a redacted edge from aggregate degree or cut-set statistics are not analysed here. This needs either a dedicated disclosure-control model or a follow-up finding; it is marked a gap rather than presented as solved.
Dependency and impact edges in this mixin are not intrinsically spatial. A host subject with geographic dependencies should compose a separate spatial model rather than extend edge semantics here.

Precedence between competing licence profiles is defined, but reconciling two contradictory edge assertions from different authoritative systems is deliberately left to the host model's generic conflict machinery; only the append-only supersession mechanism is provided locally.

known_omissions: Weighted and probabilistic propagation (impact strength decay over hops, Bayesian propagation) is not modelled. It was rejected for this pass because no cited primary source supports a general weighting semantics, and quantification belongs to the referenced risk model.
Cut-set enumeration complexity is not addressed: minimal cut-set enumeration is exponential in the general case, so the exhaustiveness marker is required but no bounding strategy is prescribed.

Centrality measures beyond degree (betweenness, PageRank, articulation points) are omitted. Only fan-in, fan-out and cut sets have direct support in the cited standards; adding others without primary grounding would be unsupported structure.

Temporal graph semantics beyond per-edge validity intervals - for example reachability over time-respecting paths, where a path is valid only if edge intervals are ordered - is identified but not modelled; it is a genuine gap that a temporal-reachability extension should close.
Multi-edge and hyperedge cases (one assertion with several targets, as SPDX permits) are carried in the data model but their effect on path and cut-set semantics is not fully specified.

The CISA Framing Software Component Transparency PDF body could not be machine-parsed in this pass, so it is cited only for the framing established on its landing page, not for internal normative claims about dependency depth or known unknowns.

The normative text of ISO/IEC 39075:2024 is paywalled; the path restrictor vocabulary was verified through the ISO catalogue entry plus implementation and secondary descriptions, not by reading the standard.
Incremental and streaming re-derivation (updating a projection from a delta rather than a full re-run) is out of this pass; only full supersession is defined.
conflicts: W3C PROV-CONSTRAINTS states there is no inference making derivation transitive, while OWL 2 permits declaring a property transitive and composing property chains. These are not reconcilable by default, so this model requires transitivity to be explicitly declared per relation type with a recorded basis, and treats any unmarked transitive claim as invalid.

SPDX attaches completeness to an individual relationship assertion, whereas CycloneDX makes a document-level statement that absence from the graph is opaque. This model uses a scoped declaration covering a frontier, which is broader than the SPDX per-relationship marker and narrower than a blanket document-level assumption; neither source is fully satisfied and the divergence is recorded rather than hidden.

RDF 1.1 Semantics establishes that a valid inference need not be materialised, while graph analytics practice routinely writes derived properties back into the graph. This model permits materialisation but forbids merging derived statements into the asserted edge set, which is stricter than common practice.

IEC 61025 and IEC 61078 use cut set and path set in a coherent-system reliability sense with defined failure semantics, whereas software dependency analysis borrows the terms structurally without failure logic. The model records the method reference and assumptions to keep the borrowed usage honest, but the terminological overlap remains a source of misreading.

Graph engines differ in default path semantics: some default to trail or simple, others to walk. ISO/IEC 39075 makes the restrictor explicit, so this model mandates declaring it, which will produce results that differ from engine defaults.
regional_assumptions: No jurisdiction-specific content is asserted. The only region-sensitive point is deletion: where a data-protection regime such as the EU GDPR right to erasure compels physical removal, the adopting Dimension's retention policy overrides the tombstone rule and the resulting gap must be recorded as a declared known unknown rather than as an absent edge.

Cited standards are English-language international or de facto standards; SPDX, CycloneDX and VEX practice is strongest in software supply chain contexts, and the mixin's generalisation to non-software dependency domains (organisational, physical, contractual) is asserted structurally and relies on the IEC dependability standards for cross-domain support.

Public-authority framing is drawn from a United States agency (CISA); comparable EU frameworks such as the Cyber Resilience Act were not examined in this pass and may impose different completeness expectations.
adversarial_checks: Attempted to justify a 'no impact' answer from a traversal alone. Rejected: CycloneDX states that objects absent from the dependency graph may have unknown dependencies and should be treated as opaque, and RDF is purely assertional with no way to state absence. The structure therefore blocks the answer unless a covering completeness declaration with the closed-world flag exists.

Tested whether transitive impact could be inferred by default from chained edges. Rejected: PROV-CONSTRAINTS explicitly declines to make derivation transitive and demonstrates that wasInformedBy is not transitive. Transitivity is modelled as a declared property with a recorded basis and depth bound, not a default.

Tested whether this model should own the evaluation and enforcement of impact rules, since it defines licence profiles. Rejected under the relation contract: a reference to an evaluator, enforcement point or audit record grants no ownership of execution, enforcement or audit semantics. The validation function returns verdicts and the registration function records externally produced runs; neither executes or enforces.

Tested whether an exclusion could simply be modelled as edge removal, which would simplify the structure. Rejected: removal would convert a policy decision into an apparent absence and would silently strengthen every downstream negative claim. Exclusions are therefore separate statements and suppressed edges must be reported as suppressed.

Tested whether path, cycle, degree and cut-set results deserve one generic 'graph metric' finding. Rejected: ISO/IEC 39075's restrictors, the closure-safety consequences of cycles and the reliability-standard framing of cut sets impose genuinely different declaration obligations, and collapsing them would let a consumer read a walk-based result as a simple-path result.

Tested whether a graph schema, storage layout or query surface belonged in scope. Rejected: storage and query are projections, and modelling them would make the mixin a graph database specification, which the boundary notes and out-of-scope list explicitly forbid.

Searched for a counterexample to deny-by-default licensing, on the argument that most dependency edges obviously propagate. Retained deny-by-default anyway: SPDX lifecycle scope establishes that a build dependency and an operational dependency carry different implications, so 'obviously propagates' is question-dependent and an unmatched edge must be reported, not assumed.
